_note: Narration script for the AO module 'Baseline obs at a high-speed MVA' (CPP-004-AO, CPP-063-AO, CTL-070 Adult RDR Chart, CTL-042 Major Trauma Tool). Lee on eleven_v4, [calmly] prefix, two takes (scenes 1-4, then 5-9) joined with 0.6 s of silence. The prompt spells SpO2, GCS, RDR, BP, ED and EOC as letters and ISBAR as 'eye-ess-bar'; captions use the text here. Scene 5 (shock) is DSY wording based on the Khan Academy video, approved by the owner 26 Oct 2026. 27 Oct 2026: the sentence 'Take at least two complete sets in the first hour.' was cut from the audio (15.336 to 18.278 s) at the owner's request; no new take.

lines.head: High-speed crash
sentences: Two or more sets show you where they're heading.

lines.head: Why a baseline
sentences: Basic care says gain, measure and record as much as you can.
That's how you see risk, deterioration, or a response to treatment.
Repeat them at least every 15 minutes.
Your first set is the baseline.
Every later set is compared with it.

lines.head: What to record
sentences: SpO2, and any oxygen you're giving.
Don't read the monitor's heart rate.

lines.head: The RDR chart
sentences: Plot every set on the RDR chart.
Each number lands in a zone.
Escalate if the zones move from yellow to red, or red to purple.
Or if any obs is purple.
Or if three or more are red or yellow.

lines.head: Shock
sentences: A bleeding patient can look fine at first.
Blood pressure can hold for a while.
Without a baseline, you won't see the climb.

lines.head: Major Trauma Tool
sentences: Check each set against the Major Trauma Tool.
It's Level 1 at any time if GCS is 13 or less.
Heart rate is under 50 or over 120.
Or the breathing rate is under 10 or over 30.
Your patient may not be Level 1 at the first set, but they might be by the third.
Go to the closest trauma service or nearest ED, with early notification.

lines.head: Temperature
sentences: Temperature is part of the baseline too.
Hypothermia happens in hot and cold weather.
The lethal triad video explains why cold matters when someone's bleeding.

lines.head: Act on the trend
sentences: When you hand over, give the trend, not just the last set.
